the use of iPSCs in the study of ALS has been a success, but that the field is in its infancy and has much to learn.

we are harnessing cellular aging to model ALS, in a bid to better understand the molecular consequences of aging on the pathogenesis of ALS.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the molecular consequences of cellular aging in iPSC‐derived motor neurons can be faithfully recapitulated in vitro by a combination of genetic and pharmacological approaches, and that the resulting phenotypes can be exploited to screen for novel therapeutic strategies in the quest to develop effective treatments for ALS.

the use of iPSC‐derived models of ALS must be considered in the light of the age of the cells, and that this is likely to be an essential consideration for the development of future therapeutic strategies.
